newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African rand plumbs new lows.
newsitem.headline: South African rand plumbs new lows.

text.p: The South African rand plumbed new lows against the dollar and British pound on Monday, hit by speculative dollar demand out of London, dealers said.
The rand stood at 4.6430/80 against the dollar -- an all-time low -- after settling at 4.6110/6160 on Friday.

Dealers said the currency was expected to push weaker on the day, possibly moving as weak as 4.65 against the greenback depending on the amount of dollars the central Reserve Bank was prepared to offer to the market.
Asked if the currency could test 4.65, one dealer said: "Unless the Reserve Bank comes in aggressively, I'll have to say yes."

He noted that the Bank had little in its armoury to defend the ailing currency. South Africa's foreign reserves have been halved in dollar terms since the end of 1995, falling from 15.7 billion rand ($4.3 billion at the prevailing rates) to 10.0 billion rand at the end of September ($2.2 billion), equivalent to just four weeks' import cover.
Against the crosses, the rand sank to yet another record low against sterling, hitting 7.4435/4633 from 7.3862 bid on Friday.

On the bond market, yields rose above the 15.80 percent level for the first time since June as sentiment was dented by the weaker rand, poor money supply data on Friday and bearishness surrounding comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals on Friday.
Stals said on Friday that the central bank might need to tighten monetary policy if there was no sign of a slowdown in bank credit extension and money supply growth.
Market commentators are fearful that an interest rate hike could stymie hopes of a 2.5 percent growth rate next year, after an expected 3.0 percent this year and 3.3 percent in 1995.
